transcript.text: My Beko keeps stopping randomly in the middle of a wash with water still in it. Sometimes it's fine for a week, then it does it twice in a day. The model starts WTG I think. I've cleaned the filter. Driving me mad.

The strongest lead is an intermittent drainage fault. A clean filter rules out the easy blockage, but the pump itself can stick intermittently, or there can be a restriction in the sump hose, drain hose or household waste pipe. Water left in the drum is why it will not move on to spin. When it next stops, try this before switching it off:
1. Select Drain/Spin. Listen for a hum, buzzing or repeated attempts from low down at the front. If it hums but does not empty, that points to a jammed/weak drain pump or a blockage beyond the filter.
2. If it empties normally on Drain/Spin, note whether it then completes the cycle. That makes an intermittent pump or drainage/level-sensing issue more likely than the main control. With the machine off and unplugged, also check that the external drain hose is not kinked, crushed behind the machine, or pushed airtight too far down its standpipe. Keep towels handy if you move it. If Drain/Spin cannot shift the water despite a clear filter and an unrestricted hose, an engineer is the sensible next step: the likely component is the drain pump, but its wiring and the internal hoses should be checked before any part is fitted.

Ok but it's not stopping right now so I can't try the Drain/Spin bit. The hose is fine though, goes into a standpipe, no kinks. Also it happens on cold washes too, not just hot. Sometimes the pump runs for a second then stops, if that helps?

That does help: a pump that starts for a second and then stops when there is water to remove points to the drain pump sticking, or to something intermittently catching at its inlet. As the filter and external hose have already been checked, the drain pump is now the leading suspect; an internal sump-hose obstruction is the next possibility. Pump wiring or the control is less likely, but cannot be ruled out yet. 1. With the machine switched off and unplugged, put towels and a shallow tray down, remove the filter, then shine a torch into the opening. Gently turn the small plastic impeller with a finger. It should move with slight magnetic notches, but not be seized, loose, or have damaged vanes. Check for hair grips, coins, fabric or debris wrapped behind it. - Anything found or a jammed impeller: clear it, refit the filter securely, then monitor the next wash. - It feels free and clear: the pump can still be failing electrically or internally under load, so it remains the likely part. If it stops with water in again and the pump only runs briefly, avoid repeatedly restarting it. An engineer should check the pump, its wiring and the internal sump hose before a pump is fitted; that is the sensible next repair route.

Hmm, I've already cleaned the filter twice and it was only fluff in there. I'm not taking the machine apart though. Is turning the impeller thing something I can do just through the filter hole, or do I need an engineer straight away?

Yes — on most washing machines the impeller can be checked through the filter opening; you do not need to remove panels or take the machine apart for that. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Put towels and a shallow tray down, as residual water may come out.
2. Remove the filter and use a torch to look through the opening. The small plastic vanes just behind it are the pump impeller.
3. Gently turn it with a finger. It should move with little magnetic “steps” or notches. It should not be solidly jammed, very loose, or have broken/missing vanes. Look for anything wrapped behind it, such as a hair grip, thread or fabric. If it is jammed or you find debris, clearing that may solve the intermittent stopping. If it feels clear and moves normally, the drain pump itself is still the most likely faulty component, with an internal sump-hose obstruction the next possibility. You do not need an engineer before doing this basic check. But if it is clear and the machine continues to stop with water inside, an engineer is the sensible next step: diagnosing the pump, internal hose and wiring requires access beyond the filter opening.

Ok, so I can just poke at it through the filter hole without opening anything up? Fine, I'll have a go. Nothing's been stuck in there before, though, just fluff. If it feels normal and still stalls, I'll get someone out I suppose.

Yes — just through the filter opening, with no panels removed. Use a torch and only a fingertip; do not force it or poke tools into it. Keep towels down and unplug the machine first. If it turns with small magnetic steps and looks intact, that would make an intermittent drain-pump failure the leading cause. If it is jammed, very loose or has damaged vanes, that points to a pump-path obstruction or failed pump instead. Given the intermittent stopping with water left inside, plus the clear filter and unkinked external hose, an engineer checking the drain pump, sump hose and pump wiring would be the sensible next route if the impeller feels normal.

candidates: Intermittent drain-pump fault or obstruction beyond the filter (high)
Heating or water-level sensing fault causing the programme to stall (low)
